quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-01.prompt:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $P \in \mathrm{Syl}_p(G)$ for some prime $p$. Suppose $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ with $|G : N| = |P| > 1$.

(i) Prove that $N$ is the subset of $G$ consisting of all elements of order not divisible by $p$.

(ii) If the elements of $G$ outside of $N$ all have $p$-power order, prove that $P$ is its own normalizer.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-01.answer: (i) $|N|$ is prime to $p$ and $G/N\cong P$ is a $p$-group, so $p'$-elements map to $1$ in $G/N$. (ii) A Sylow $q$-subgroup $Q$ ($q\ne p$) of $N_G(P)$ lies in $N$, so $[Q,P]\subseteq N\cap P=1$; if $Q\ne1$, $xy$ with $o(x)=q$, $o(y)=p$ has order $pq$ and lies outside $N$. Hence $N_G(P)$ is a $p$-group, equal to $P$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-02.prompt:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P$ be a prime ideal of $R$. If $V$ is a (right) $R$-module, define
$$W = \{ v \in V \mid va = 0 \text{ for some } a \in R \setminus P \}$$
where $R \setminus P$ is the set of elements of $R$ not in $P$.

(i) Show that $W$ is an $R$-submodule of $V$.

(ii) If $R$ is Noetherian and $V$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, prove that $Wb = 0$ for some $b \in R \setminus P$.

(iii) If $V$ is a simple $R$-module and $W = 0$, prove that $P$ is a maximal ideal.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-02.answer: (i) $R\setminus P$ is multiplicatively closed: $v_1a_1=v_2a_2=0\Rightarrow(v_1+v_2)a_1a_2=0$. (ii) $W$ is finitely generated; multiply the annihilating elements of its generators. (iii) $\mathrm{ann}(v)$ is maximal for $0\ne v\in V$ and misses $R\setminus P$, so $\mathrm{ann}(v)\subseteq P$, forcing $P=\mathrm{ann}(v)$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-03.prompt:
Let $E$ be a splitting field of the polynomial $x^3 - 2$ over the rationals $\mathbb{Q}$, and assume that $E$ is contained in the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. Let $F = E \cap \mathbb{R}$ be the real subfield of $E$, and note that $F = \mathbb{Q}[\sqrt[3]{2}]$.

(i) Show that $G = \mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ contains an element $\sigma$ with the property that the only elements of $F$ fixed by $\sigma$ are rational.

(ii) Let $a \in F$ and suppose that $a^3 \in \mathbb{Q}$. Show that one of $a$, $a\sqrt[3]{2}$, or $a\sqrt[3]{4}$ is contained in $\mathbb{Q}$.

(iii) Prove that $\sqrt[3]{3} \notin E$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-03.answer: (i) Take $\sigma$ of order 3, $\sigma(\sqrt[3]2)=\omega\sqrt[3]2$: its fixed field $\mathbb Q(\omega)$ has degree $2$, so it meets $F$ (degree 3) in $\mathbb Q$. (ii) $\sigma(a)=\omega^{-i}a$, so $\sigma$ fixes $a\sqrt[3]2^{\,i}\in F$. (iii) Otherwise $\sqrt[3]3\in F$ and one of $\sqrt[3]3,\sqrt[3]6,\sqrt[3]{12}$ would be rational.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-04.prompt: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix over a field $K$ and assume that the characteristic polynomial of $A$ has distinct roots in the algebraic closure of $K$. Prove that any two $n\times n$ $K$-matrices which commute with A must commute with each other.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-04.answer: Over $\bar K$, $A=PDP^{-1}$ with $D$ diagonal with distinct entries; the centralizer of $D$ is the diagonal matrices ($z_{ij}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)=0$), which commute with each other.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-05.prompt:
Let $S = M_n(F)$ be the ring of $n \times n$ matrices over the field $F$.

(i) If $s \in S$ is nilpotent, prove that the trace of $s$ is zero.

(ii) Suppose $R$ is a ring and that $\theta\colon R \to S$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$ with the property that every element of $I$ is a sum of nilpotent elements of $R$. Show that $\theta(I) = 0$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1994f-05.answer: (i) All eigenvalues (in $\bar F$) of a nilpotent matrix are $0$, and the trace is their sum. (ii) $\theta(I)$ is an ideal of the simple ring $S$ on which the trace vanishes, so it does not contain $e_{11}$; hence $\theta(I)\ne S$ and $\theta(I)=0$.
